question: Should OpenClaw treat fixed HealthKit aggregates as an approved health/fitness service and send them through the gateway to the configured model provider and chat history after two explicit user opt-ins?
rationale: Repository policy requires maintainers to own sensitive-data and configuration boundaries; source inspection can validate the architecture but cannot decide whether this product purpose, third-party disclosure, and retention model are acceptable.

options.title: Approve bounded summaries
options.body: Approve only fixed periods and aggregate fields with explicit iOS consent, provider/history disclosure and revocation, and gateway dangerous-command opt-in.

options.title: Require local-only presentation
options.body: Permit summaries in the iOS UI but prohibit gateway or model-provider transmission until a stronger privacy architecture exists.

options.title: Keep HealthKit out of core
options.body: Decline first-party HealthKit access and leave health integrations outside the shipped app.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded summaries
recommendation.body: Approve only fixed periods and aggregate fields with explicit iOS consent, provider/history disclosure and revocation, and gateway dangerous-command opt-in.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored and is assigned to the focused proposal and has the strongest recent history on the gateway policy boundary.
